findings.before: The Judean teachers make Mosaic circumcision necessary for salvation; Paul warns people seeking justification by law that receiving circumcision makes them obligated to the whole law and severed from Christ. The letter is a separate argument, not a verbatim report of these teachers or this meeting.
findings.after: The Judean teachers make Mosaic circumcision necessary for salvation. Galatians states whole-law obligation for one receiving circumcision and warns those seeking justification by law of separation from Christ. Its distinct clauses and conditions remain a separate argument rather than a verbatim report of these teachers or a blanket claim about every circumstance of circumcision.
findings.fix: Preserve the separate scope of Galatians5:3 and5:4 rather than merging every circumcision circumstance with the law-justification warning.
findings.resolution: Applied in the stable preview and confirmed in the final183-unit primary; all source/target identities and counts are unchanged.

review_notes: All80 complete original source bodies,80 individual rationales and all80 retained actual target/context comparisons were independently read in four complete ordered views of5753,4878,5450 and5550 tokens. The review keeps the Judean teachers, Pharisaic believers, council speakers, letter writers and later Jerusalem speakers distinct. The two Galatians conditions, public/private presentations and possible Jerusalem visits are not collapsed into one unreported chronology.
